LEARNING PATH LESSON · SIGHT WORDS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

The — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

Five minutes, one card: say “the” clearly, use it in a real sentence (“The cat sat on the mat.”) and finish with one small game.

What it means

It points at the one particular thing we mean.

How to teach it

  1. Hold up the card and read “the” slowly, sliding a finger under it. Point out its shape: three letters marching left to right: a tall t, a tall h and a little e.
  2. Ask your child to find the first letter on the canvas and draw a ring around it, then say the whole word.
  3. Play the game below, say “the” one last time and stop while it is still fun.

How to say it

Start with th, tongue tip resting lightly between your teeth, then a quick uh. Before a vowel sound it often turns into thee, as in the apple.

Where to use it

Say it in a real sentence: “The cat sat on the mat.” Then try “Please close the door.” Where to spot it: titles like The Zoo and The End, and almost every line of a story.

Try this game

Ask for things by name: pass me the cup, hand me the spoon. Each time, your child holds up the card when they hear the.

Understanding check

Tomorrow, show the card and say nothing. If your child reads “the” at once, it has arrived; if not, play the game again the day after.

Parent tips

Do not drill “the” on its own for long. Slip it into the books you read today and let the story do the practicing.

This lesson pairs with the The flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Sight Words (Class 29).
